newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola ends higher on CBOT spillover.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola ends higher on CBOT spillover.

text.p: WCE canola futures ended higher Thursday in response to gains in CBOT soybeans and commercial buying, while feedgrains settled up on weather-related concerns, WCE traders said.
"There was commerical buying on the close in May, but the real reason we're up is the strength from Chicago," said a floor trader.
CBOT soy futures were sharply higher in response to stronger-than-expected export sales and expectations for a cut to 1996-97 soybean ending stocks in Friday's supply and demand forecasts from USDA.
WCE canola closed up $1.80 to $4.20, with May up $4.20 at $426.40. Flaxseed closed up 0.20 to $1.50 higher on commercial buying with July up $0.70 at $349.70.
Western barley features also settled higher, but volume was described as very light. Traders said commericals were spreading July/October and July/December.
Feed wheat futures closed higher in sympathy with CBOT corn and wheat and in response to ideas that wintry weather might delay plantings, traders said.
Wheat closed up $1.30 to $1.90 with July up $1.90 at $168.30. July western barley settled $1.70 higher at $140.30.
Oats and feed peas stayed tradeless, traders said.
(All values in Canadian dollars, except feed peas)
